A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TOMATO benchmark and contain complete main texts and Appendices A–L. Text, tables, equations, and figures support reliable comparison, including content merged or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original model and human evaluations, comparisons across five benchmarks, scenario analyses, and extensive model failure cases.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluations of eight models and a low-frame-count experiment in Appendix C.3.

M1.justification: Benchmark construction, annotation, and the zero-shot inference and answer-extraction procedures remain unchanged. The additional models are evaluated comparison systems; no new model, training algorithm, or inference method is proposed.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,484-question, 1,417-video TOMATO benchmark, six tasks, and human-centric, real-world, and simulated scenarios. VITATECS, MVBench, TempCompass, and ReXTime remain the comparison benchmarks. Added models and frame counts do not introduce new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Table 7 substantially expands the evaluated model set from 23 to 31 while retaining all earlier comparators. Additions are Gemini 1.5 Pro, Gemini 2.0 Flash Exp, Claude 3 Haiku, Qwen2-VL-2B, LLaVA-Video-72B, LLaVA-Video-7B, LLaVA-Video-7B-Video-Only, and AuroraCap-7B-VID.

E3.justification: V2 adds a Qwen2-VL-72B evaluation at 0, 1, 2, 4, 6, and 8 frames across five benchmarks. It also revises the three evaluation metrics by adding epsilon to their denominators. Existing sampling and zero-shot protocols remain unchanged; unchanged Tables 3–6 do not establish that scores were recomputed using the revised formulas.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.3 examines Qwen2-VL-72B accuracy with low frame counts, extending the existing frame-count sensitivity analysis. The counterfactual, zoom, viewpoint, and simulated-human analyses are retained, as are all failure cases in Appendices G–L.

E5.justification: Table 9 retains the same seed disclosures, including seed 215 for GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini. Neither version adds repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; the additional results follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 7 adds six-task and overall scores for eight models, including overall accuracies of 36.1 for Gemini 1.5 Pro and 33.7 for Gemini 2.0 Flash Exp. LLaVA-Video-72B becomes the open-source visual-cues leader at 50.0, above Qwen2-VL-72B's unchanged 48.6. All earlier Table 7 scores remain unchanged. Appendix C.3 adds accuracy curves, and Table 2 revises task percentages, such as rotation from 21.4% to 19.3%, matching the retained question counts.

T1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 revise the mathematical definitions of Multi-Frame Gain, Frame Order Sensitivity, and Frame Information Disparity by adding a small positive epsilon to each denominator. This makes the ratios defined when denominator accuracy is zero. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: three benchmarking principles, TOMATO, the substantial human-model gap, and failures to interpret frames continuously. Updating the evaluated model count broadens supporting evidence without changing these claims.

C2.justification: New Section 6.4 explicitly qualifies scenario findings as exploratory because the videos were not designed to rigorously validate them. The viewpoint discussion adds an interpretation concerning the absence of a main subject. V2 also removes the separate paragraph arguing that the proprietary/open-source gap is narrowing.

D1.justification: Table 9 adds checkpoints and generation settings for seven newly evaluated models, including AuroraCap's token_kept_ratio of 0.61. Table 1 adds video-resolution statistics. Existing hardware, prompts, and code-access information remain. Documentation is incomplete for the expanded evaluation: Qwen2-VL-2B lacks a configuration row.

R1.justification: Section 3 adds explicit connections to prior work on single-frame bias, frame shuffling, and temporal information, citing Lei, Misra, Dorkenwald, Hao, Huang, and Liu. References for AuroraCap and LLaVA-Video are added, while the separate GPT-4o-mini reference is removed. The central positioning against existing video benchmarks remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized grammatical edits and paragraph reductions, divides the analysis into Main Analysis and Scenario Analysis, adds acknowledgments, and updates the publication header. The overall narrative and extensive appendix organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V1 Figures 2–4 are consolidated into the three panels of v2 Figure 2, with the human/simulation example rearranged. V2 adds the Appendix C.3 plot, expands tables, and clarifies captions, including correcting Table 6's input description. Other figures and appendix displays are retained with renumbering and styling changes.

improvement.justification: V2 provides broader comparative evidence and a finer frame-count analysis while better qualifying exploratory scenario findings. Table 2 also aligns task percentages with the existing question counts. These are useful incremental gains rather than a resolution of a major scientific deficiency. Incomplete new-model configuration coverage and the older percentages retained in Appendix C.1 limit the cleanup.
